<noinclude><pagequality level="2" user="Sabababanana" /></noinclude><section begin="par10" />p, 71 f.), the {{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph}} is ''necessary''<ref>See Delitzsch, ‘Bemerkungen über masoretisch treue Darstellung des alttestam. Textes,’ in the {{GHGcite|title=Ztschr. f. luth. Theol. u. Kirche}}, vol. xxiv. 1863, p. 409 ff.</ref> when, in a strengthened {{GHGterm|medial}} consonant with {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} (consequently not in cases like {{GHGheb|text=וַיְהִי}}, &c.), preceded by a Pathaḥ, the sign of the strengthening ({{GHGterm|Dageš forte}}) has fallen away, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=הַֽלֲלוּ}} (but ed. Mant. and Ginsb. {{GHGheb|text=הַלְלוּ|translate=praise ye!}} {{GHGheb|text=וַתְּאַֽלֲצֵהוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=16|verse=16}}; no less universally, where after a consonant with {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} the same consonant follows (to separate them more sharply, and hence with a {{GHGterm|Metheg}} always preceding), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=סוֹרֲרִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=68|verse=9}}; {{GHGheb|text=קִֽלֲלָֽתְךָ}} (ed. Mant. and Ginsb. {{GHGheb|text=קִלְל׳}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=13}} (but not without exceptions, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=חִקְקֵי־}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=10|verse=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=צִלְלֵי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=6|verse=4}}, and so always {{GHGheb|text=הִנְנִי|translate=behold me}}, {{GHGheb|text=הִנְנוּ|translate=behold us}}; on {{GHGheb|text=כְ}} before the suffix {{GHGheb|text=ךָ}}, see {{GHGpar|20|b}}); also in certain forms under ''Kaph'' and ''Rêš'' after a long vowel and before the tone, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=תֹּֽאכֲלֶ֫נָּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=3|verse=17}}; {{GHGheb|text=בָּֽרֲכִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=103|verse=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַתְּשָֽׁרֲתֵ֫הוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=1|verse=4}} (but {{GHGheb|text=וְיִתְבָּ֫רְכוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=72|verse=17}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=4|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=29|verse=20}}, because the tone is thrown back on to the ''ā''. After {{GHGterm|ē Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}} remains even before the tone, as {{GHGheb|text=בֵּֽרְכוּ}} &c.; but before Maqqef {{GHGheb|text=אֵֽלֲכָה־נָּא}} Baer {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=4|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=15|verse=7}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=40|verse=15}}, but ed. Mant., Jabl., Ginsb. {{GHGheb|text=אֵֽלְ׳}})<ref>On the uncertainty of the MSS. in some cases which come under {{GHGpar|10|a|nonumber=1}}, see {{GHGcite|title=Minḥat shay}} (the Masoretic comm. in ed. Mant.) on {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=12|verse=3}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=7|verse=6}}.</ref>; (''b'') under initial sibilants after {{GHGheb|text=וּ}} copulative, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=וּֽזֲהַב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=12}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=48|verse=20}}; {{GHGheb|text=וּֽסֲחַר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=45|verse=14}}; {{GHGheb|text=וּֽשֲׂדֵה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Lv|chapter=25|verse=34}}; {{GHGheb|text=וּֽשֲׁקָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=26}}; {{GHGheb|text=וּֽשֲׁמָע}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=23|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=37|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=9|verse=18}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=14|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=9|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=14|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ec|chapter=9|verse=7}}—to emphasize the vocal character of the {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ}}. For the same reason under the emphatic {{GHGheb|text=ט}} in {{GHGheb|text=הֽוּטֲלוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=22|verse=28}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=33|verse=25}}; after ''Qôph'' in {{GHGheb|text=וּֽקֲדָרְתִּי}} (so Baer, but ed. Mant., Jabl., Ginsb. {{GHGheb|text=וּקְ׳}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=23|verse=41}}; {{GHGheb|text=וּֽקֲרָב־}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=55|verse=22}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer.|chapter=32|verse=9}}; under ''Rêš'' in {{GHGheb|text=אֵֽרֲדָה}} (ed. Mant. {{GHGheb|text=אֵֽרְ׳}}). {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=21}}; {{GHGheb|text=וּֽרֲעֵם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=28|verse=9}}; even under {{GHGheb|text=ת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Eze|chapter=26|verse=21}}<ref>{{GHGcritic|{{GHGheb|text=וּֽתֲבֻֿקְשִׁׄי}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Eze|chapter=26|verse=21}} in Aleppo codex.|Amire80}}</ref>; under {{GHGheb|text=ב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=2|verse=8}}; {{GHGheb|text=וּבֵֽרֲכֶךָּ}} so Jabl., Ginsb., but ed. Mant. {{GHGheb|text=וּבֵֽרְ׳}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=24|verse=13}}; (''c'') under sonants, sibilants or ''Qôph'' after ''ĭ'', e.g. {{GHGheb|text=יִֽצֲחַק}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=21|verse=6}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=30|verse=38|hidebook=1}} and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=21|verse=28}} (under {{GHGheb|text=ק}}); {{GHGheb|text=אִֽמֲרוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=12|verse=7}}; {{GHGheb|text=הֲתִֽמֲלֹךְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=22|verse=15}}; {{GHGheb|text=כִֽנֲרוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=11|verse=2}}; {{GHGheb|text=בִּֽסֲבָךְ־}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=74|verse=5}}, —for the same reason as the cases under ''b''<ref>Ben-Asher requires {{GHGheb|text=־ֲ}} for {{GHGheb|text=־ְ}} (even for {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ quiescens}}) generally before a guttural or {{GHGheb|text=ר}}; hence Baer reads in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=15|verse=5}} {{GHGheb|text=בִּֽקַרָב־}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=אֶֽקֲרָא}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=49|verse=15|nonumber=1}} {{GHGheb|text=לִֽשֲׁאוֹל}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=65|verse=5|nonumber=1}} {{GHGheb|text=תִּֽבֲחַר}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=68|verse=24|nonumber=1}} {{GHGheb|text=תִּֽמֲחַץ}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=30|verse=17}} {{GHGheb|text=תִּֽלֲעַג}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=29|verse=25}} {{GHGheb|text=אֶֽבֲחַר}}; cf. Delitzsch, ''Psalms'', 12:7, note.</ref>; according to Baer also in {{GHGheb|text=שִֽׁפֲמוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=30|verse=28}}; {{GHGheb|text=יִֽפְגָֽשֲׁךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=18}} after ''ŏ'' (cf. {{GHGpar|9|v}}), as well as after ''a'' in {{GHGheb|text=הַֽקֲשִׁיבָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=9|verse=19}}; {{GHGheb|text=הַֽבֲרָכָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=27|verse=38}}; {{GHGheb|text=הַֽמֲצֹרָעִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=7|verse=8}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|10|h}}
'''B'''. The {{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph-Qameṣ}} is less restricted to the gutturals than the first two, and stands more frequently for a simple {{GHGterm|Š<sup>e</sup>wâ mobile}} when an original O-sound requires to be partly preserved, e.g. at the beginning, in {{GHGheb|text=רֳאִי}} (ground-form {{GHGpron|rŏʾy}}) {{GHGtranslate|vision}} (cf. {{GHGpar|93|z}}); {{GHGheb|text=כֳּנַנְיָהוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=31|verse=12}}, &c., {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}} (''K<sup>e</sup>eth.'' {{GHGheb|text=כונ״}}); {{GHGheb|text=עַמֳּנִיּוֹת|translate=Ammonitish women}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=11|verse=1}} (sing. {{GHGheb|text=עַמּוֹנִית}}); {{GHGheb|text=יִרְדֳּפֶ֑ךָ}} for the usual {{GHGheb|text=יִרְדְּפֶ֑ךָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=35|verse=6}}, from {{GHGheb|text=יִרְדֹּף}}; {{GHGheb|text=תִקֳּבֶ֫נּוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=23|verse=25}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=31|verse=33}}, and elsewhere before suffixes, cf. {{GHGpar|60|a}}; {{GHGheb|text=קָדְקֳדוֹ|translate=his pate}} (from {{GHGheb|text=קָדְקֹד}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=7|verse=17}}, &c.; {{GHGheb|text=אֶשְׁקֳטָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=18|verse=4}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}. Further, like {{GHGheb|text=־ֲ}}, it stands under consonants, which ought to have {{GHGterm|Dageš forte}}, as in {{GHGheb|text=לֻֽקֳחָה}} (for {{GHGheb|text=לֻקְּחָה}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=23}}. In this example, as in {{GHGheb|text=וּֽסֳעָ֫דָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=13|verse=7}}; {{GHGheb|text=וּֽסֳאָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=7|verse=18}}; and {{GHGheb|text=וּֽצֳעָ֫קִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=22|verse=20}}, the {{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph-Qameṣ}} is no doubt due to the influence of the<section end="par10" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
